svg.title: HyperWeave — Spectral Terminal Field
svg.desc: HyperWeave footer on the Spectral Terminal Field substrate: a 150 by 14 monospace terminal lattice at a 1 to 2 cell aspect, every cell assigned a palette token rather than a sampled gradient, with HYPERWEAVE in Orbitron overprinted at maximum density in the core emission token.

hw:chromatic.theory: thermal-diffusion-matrix — token-quantized lattice, no gradient primitives

hw:motion.vocabulary: thermal-diffusion sweep — 30 degree shear on the subsurface bloom, phosphor cascade running top to bottom across the lattice

hw:material.surface: monospace terminal lattice over subsurface bloom

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: Implement the supplied Spectral Terminal Field DNA as written, rather than approximating it — exact tokens, the declared glyph ramp, the declared cell aspect, and the declared area weights.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: The correction that mattered is anti_gradient_ai. The previous pass painted the lattice by masking a blurred field, which meant every glyph took a sampled gradient colour — a gradient in everything but name. Here colour is a token decision per cell and nothing else: the field is evaluated at each cell centre, and the cells are then quantile-cut at the DNA's own declared weights, so the measured area distribution matches the spec by construction rather than by tuning. Measured against spec: void 945/2100=0.450 vs 0.45 | cobalt 252/2100=0.120 vs 0.12 | cyan 168/2100=0.080 vs 0.08 | incandescent 252/2100=0.120 vs 0.12 | amber 378/2100=0.180 vs 0.18 | cinnabar 105/2100=0.050 vs 0.05. Glyph level is quantile-cut too, which guarantees the whole declared ramp is exercised instead of saturating at the densest character the way the clamped build did. The ladders differ between the two DNAs and the implementation follows that: this one is a spectral ladder driven by position, cold at the left flank through the thermal core to the flare edge. Cell aspect is exactly 1 to 2 at 8 by 16 on a 224 tall canvas, which is why the frame gained four pixels over the previous 220. Runs of same-token cells are emitted as one text element pinned with textLength and spacingAndGlyphs to its exact cell span, so the lattice measures true on any monospace stack. Void cells emit no glyph at all. The wordmark is maximum overprint — the same lattice at full density in the core emission token behind an Orbitron clip.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: The subsurface bloom is still a blur, which is the one place a smooth ramp survives; the DNA asks for it by name under color_bleed_method, and it is built from blurred solid ellipses so the file contains no gradient primitive, but a strict reading of anti-gradient would delete it and lose the bleed the references clearly have. Token weights are matched as cell-count share, not as covered pixel area — a dash covers far less of its cell than an at-sign, so the true inked area of the light tokens is below their declared weight and no quantile cut can fix that without weighting by glyph coverage. The per-zone density hints in the DNA, sparse_to_medium and dense_overprint and medium_linear, are approximated by the shape of the intensity field rather than enforced zone by zone; the zones themselves are not modelled as regions. The declared ramp for this DNA is used verbatim including its ordering, which places 8 before S before 0 in one and 0 before S in the other — visually those three are near-identical in density, so two ramp steps do almost no work. Fourteen rows means the wordmark is sampled by about five rows of cells, so the overprint is coarse by construction. And the lattice does not reflow: below 1200 the cells condense with the viewBox instead of re-flowing to fewer columns.
hw:reasoning.hw:spatial-notes: Canvas 1200x224. Lattice 150 columns by 14 rows, cell 8 by 16 for a 1:2 aspect, baseline at 0.74 of row pitch, font-size 16 with each run pinned by textLength. Ramp 11 levels as declared. HYPERWEAVE in Orbitron wght 700 at 103px with 0.10em tracking, centred x600 baseline y150, measured width 977.4. Phosphor period 9.4s with row delays staggered top to bottom.
